_note: Fictional travel and expense policy for a fictional company (Northwind Labs). Each passage is one retrieved chunk. Ids are stable; cite them.

passages.title: Travel policy, section 2.1: Booking flights
passages.text: Book all flights through the company travel portal at least 14 days before departure. Economy class is the default for every employee. Flights longer than 6 hours in the air may be booked in premium economy with written approval from your director.

passages.title: Travel policy, section 2.4: Hotels
passages.text: Hotel stays are reimbursed up to the nightly cap for the destination city listed in the rate table. Room upgrades are not reimbursable unless the standard room is unavailable and you note this on the expense report. Loyalty points earned on business stays belong to the employee.

passages.title: Expense policy, section 4.2: Meals
passages.text: While traveling, meals are reimbursed up to a daily limit of 75 US dollars, including tips. Alcohol is not reimbursable. Team meals with a client present follow the client entertainment rules in section 4.5 instead.

passages.title: Expense policy, section 4.7: Receipts and deadlines
passages.text: Submit expense reports within 30 days of the end of a trip. Attach an itemized receipt for every expense of 25 US dollars or more. Reports submitted after 60 days require approval from the finance controller.

passages.title: Expense policy, section 4.9: Mileage
passages.text: Personal car use for business travel is reimbursed per mile at the rate published by finance each January. Commuting between home and your usual office is not reimbursable.

passages.title: Travel FAQ (2023, archived)
passages.text: Q: Can I book business class? A: Yes, any flight over 4 hours may be booked in business class without approval. Note: this FAQ predates the 2025 travel policy.
